newsitem.title: USA: Olsten Q4 warning buries shrs, group falls.
newsitem.headline: Olsten Q4 warning buries shrs, group falls.

text.p: Olsten Corp's Thursday pre-announcement of weaker-than-expected fourth quarter results shocked investors out the stock, pushing the shares -- and other temporary-employment issues -- into a freefall.
In unusally active trade, Olsten shares topped the NYSE net losers list with a 4-7/8 decline to 15. Early in the session it touched a new all-time low of 14-1/2.

"It is company-specific, but Olsten is one of the bigs in the group so market psychology is that if one of the leaders is having problems, how can the others do well?" said Brian Finnerty, Unterberg Harris managing director.
Finnerty, who trades the temporary-help group, added, "It is throwing out the baby with the bathwater."
Strong agreement among market bears pushed Olsten and other companies in the same business to the front of the NYSE percentage-losers pack.
Olsten's market value fell 25 percent, the most severe decline on the NYSE in trade ahead of midsession. AccuStaff Inc was second with a 15.4 percent drop, down 3-5/8 to 19-7/8.
Among other temporary-help companies, Interim Services Inc fell 8.6 percent, down 3-3/8 to 35-3/4, and Norrell Corp lost 6.2 percent, down 1-1/2 to 22-3/4.
Manpower Inc declined 3.5 percent, or 1-1/8, to 30-3/4; Kelly Services Inc, surrended one percent, or 1/4, to 27-1/4, and Robert Half International Inc was off 5.9 percent, or 2-1/4, to 36.

Earlier today Olsten said continuing margin pressure at it two primary businesses and reduced revenues from Medicare operations would trim earnings to a lower-than-expected $0.20 per share for the fourth quarter and about $1.30 per share for the year.
The projections exlude merger, integration and other non-recurring charges, Olsten said.
